A LETTER TO THE CLASS OF 2027… AND EVERY STUDENT WHO FOLLOWS

https://linktr.ee/THEWEALTHLABYO

This may be the most important letter I’ve ever written.

Not because it’s about me.

Because it’s about you.

It’s about every student wondering if what they’re learning today will actually help them tomorrow.

Let’s be honest…

Schools taught many of us how to find the square root—but not always how to read a credit report.

We learned about the Boston Tea Party—but not always why overdraft fees can empty a bank account.

Somewhere along the way, life became the teacher… and tuition became expensive.

That doesn’t have to be the story for the Class of 2027.

This letter is my promise that your future matters enough to fight for, prepare for and invest in.

Whether you’re a student, parent, grandparent, educator, coach or community leader, this letter belongs to you too.

Because every generation has one responsibility:

Leave the next generation better prepared than we were.

Take a few minutes.

Read the letter.

Talk about it.

Challenge it.

Most importantly, ask the young people in your life one question:

“What kind of future do you want?”

Their answer may change all of ours.

Welcome to THE W.E.A.L.T.H. LAB.

FUND THE REQUIREMENT. FUND THE FUTURE.

The death of the Mirabal Sisters is closely related to International Women’s Day. The Mirabal Sisters were three Dominican sisters who fought against the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo in the Dominican Republic in the 1960s.

Patria, Minerva and María Teresa Mirabal

They were arrested, tortured and murdered on November 25, 1960 for their political activism and their struggle for justice and equality.

Commemoration

In 1981, the United Nations (UN) declared March 8 as International Women’s Day, in honor of the struggles and achievements of women around the world.

In 1999, the UN also declared November 25 as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, in memory of the Mirabal Sisters.

Legacy

The Mirabal Sisters became symbols of the struggle for equality and justice for women around the world. Her legacy inspires women to fight for their rights and work towards a more equitable future.

In short, the death of the Mirabal Sisters is remembered on International Women’s Day as a reminder of the ongoing struggle for equality and justice for women, and as a tribute to their courage and sacrifice.
